thesis: Workday (Nasdaq: WDAY), fiscal year ends Jan 31. Q2 FY27 10-Q (quarter to 2026-07-31, filed 2026-08-27; statements, cover, debt, buyback, tax notes read via WebFetch; MD&A not retrievable) and 8-Ks of 2026-09-29, 2026-10-01, 2026-10-13, 2026-10-23 read. Revenue Q2 2,649M vs 2,348M (+12.8%); subscription 2,471M vs 2,169M (+13.9%); subscription backlog 27.4B, 9.0B within 12 months. TTM to 2026-07-31 (FY26 + 6M27 - 6M26): revenue 9,552+5,191-4,588 = 10,155M; GAAP operating income 721+651-287 = 1,085M (10.7%); NI 693+854-296 = 1,251M but 6M27 NI includes a 172M tax benefit (Q2 305M benefit from an intra-entity IP transfer, 374M deferred tax asset), so NI is inflated; OCF 2,939+1,215-1,073 = 3,081M; capex 162+139-64 = 237M; FCF 2,844M; SBC 1,626+871-851 = 1,646M, FCF after SBC 1,198M. Shares about 241M (196M Class A + 45M Class B, cover 2026-08-25) x 182.80 = market cap about 44.1B = 35x TTM NI (tax-flattered), 15.5x TTM FCF (6.5% yield; 2.7% after SBC), 4.3x TTM revenue. Cash 661M + marketable securities 2,742M = 3,403M vs 3.0B senior notes at 3 July 31; 2026-10-23 issued 2.5B notes at 5.70% to 6.50% (2029 to 2036) to retire the 1.0B 3.5% 2027 notes; new 1.5B revolver (2031) undrawn. 6M27 buybacks 2,907M, new 4.0B authorization in August 2026. Restructuring 8-K 2026-09-29: about 2.5% of workforce, 65M to 80M charges. Stock closed 182.80 on 11-17, down 5.8% from 194.06 on 11-16. Price implies low-teens growth continues with margins expanding; the evidence for a different view is the 27.4B backlog and 6.5% FCF yield pre-SBC.
counterthesis: Owner earnings are much lower than headline FCF: SBC is 16% of revenue and the buyback (2.9B in 6M) mostly offsets dilution; FCF after SBC yield is 2.7%. GAAP operating margin is only about 11%. Net income is flattered by a one-time deferred tax asset. New notes carry 5.7% to 6.5% coupons, about double the retiring 3.5% to 3.8% notes, so the company is raising debt to fund buybacks at a high cost; debt rises from 3.0B to about 5.5B before the 2027 retirement. AI agents may pressure seat-based HCM and finance software; growth near 13% with a restructuring and ConductorOne identity acquisition (price undisclosed) suggests defence of position. Cause of the 5.8% drop on 11-17 unknown.
invalidation: Thesis fails if subscription growth falls below about 10%, 12-month backlog growth stalls, FCF after SBC falls below about 1.0B, or debt-funded buybacks continue with margins flat.
